bibliography.abstract: Image geolocation aims to infer the geographic origin of an image from visual content alone. However, this task remains challenging in regions where countries share similar urban, roadside, architectural, and environmental characteristics. Many existing geolocation models focus on coordinate level prediction or classification performance while providing limited insight into how visual evidence contributes to location predictions. This study presents an explainable country level image geolocation pipeline for 11 ASEAN countries. First, we collected 4,850 images from GeoGuessr style sources, Google Images, and additional street level imagery. We then evaluated three approaches on this dataset: CLIP zero shot classification, a LightGBM classifier, and an MLP classifier. The MLP achieved the best test performance, attaining an accuracy and F1 score of 85.91%. For explainability, predictions generated by the MLP classifier were analyzed post hoc using CLIP attention rollout, YOLO26 object detection on the original images, and Energy Based Pointing Game (EBPG) overlap metrics. Object level analysis indicates that frequently detected objects are not necessarily associated with the highest attention density, suggesting that object frequency and attention based visual evidence capture different aspects of a scene. These results demonstrate that the proposed model can support accurate regional image geolocation while enabling object level inspection of the visual cues underlying its predictions.
bibliography.title: GeoSEAN: Explainable Country-Level Image Geolocation for ASEAN Regions

en.caveats: The evaluation relies on a relatively small dataset of 4,850 images sourced from GeoGuessr, Google Images, and street-level imagery, which may not fully represent the diverse visual landscapes of the 11 ASEAN nations.
en.what: Researchers developed GeoSEAN, an explainable country-level image geolocation pipeline tested on a newly compiled dataset of 4,850 images across 11 ASEAN countries. Evaluating three approaches, an MLP classifier achieved the highest performance with an accuracy and F1-score of 85.91%, outperforming CLIP zero-shot and LightGBM models. Post-hoc explainability analyses using CLIP attention rollout, YOLO object detection, and Energy-Based Pointing Game metrics revealed that the most frequently detected objects do not always align with the highest visual attention density.
en.why: It establishes a benchmark for regional image geolocation in Southeast Asia, where shared architectural and environmental features make country-level distinction difficult, while demonstrating that object frequency and attention-based visual cues capture distinct, non-overlapping aspects of geographic evidence.
